# AT4532 bench frame, 2026-09-28

`at4532_tcp32_20260928.hex` contains exactly 694 captured bytes. Source:
`ThermoPower-diagnostic-5 (1).zip`, `protocol-results.json`, temperature transaction
at `2026-09-28T19:58:56.695561+00:00` (0.6.5, build `57068aea`).

Forensic reconstruction uses **only captured bytes**:
`transaction_boundary.pending_before_tx_hex` (six bytes, `TCP-32`) followed by
`rx_bytes` (688 bytes, beginning `,T:`, ending CRLF). It is not an instruction to
repair frames inside the product or associate old bytes with a new FETCH.

SHA-256 of the decoded 694 bytes:
`43a25e7339ed9ee447e7c6a880b526956cf3afe49c22d545489f00013cd8dff5`.

CP936, 69 fields, 32 primary channels, CH01–CH24 Open, CH25–CH32 numeric.
The 34 auxiliary fields remain opaque. The original diagnostic ZIP, device inventory,
operator information and complete logs are not included in the repository.

Tests replay the real frame and derive distinct timestamps only for explicitly
synthetic soak responses. Automated replay is not physical homologation.
